title: Renewal pricing portability and granular uplift allocator playbook
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: Large enterprise customers often have multi-product usage that doesn't map cleanly to a single renewal true-up calculation. Current uplift rules are coarse (flat % across products) and cause friction during negotiations and over/under-charging after term. Goal: Design a repeatable framework that (1) distributes renewal uplift across multiple product lines (portability), (2) smooths true-ups across renewal windows to reduce invoice shock, and (3) provides a configurable allocator that ties uplift to observed usage signals and contract guardrails. Deliverables: a playbook (decision matrix), PRD for billing and contract language, an A/B experiment plan for uplift bands, and a rollout path for enterprise contracts and renewal ops.
acceptance_criteria: Decision matrix that maps product groups to uplift allocation rules (percent weights) for top-30 enterprise customers
A PRD and example contract language for 1-year and 3-year renewals including portability clauses
An experiment plan with at least two uplift band treatments and tracking on NRR, renewal conversion, and dispute rate
Implementation checklist for billing to support smoothing (monthly amortized true-ups) and exportable audit logs
approach_and_tradeoffs: Option A: Weight-based allocator — allocate uplift by historical spend percentage. Pros: predictable, simple. Cons: perpetuates historical product concentration.

Option B: Signal-based allocator — use trailing-90-day active-user and token velocity signals plus a minimum floor. Pros: aligns uplift with current growth. Cons: needs validation and additional data engineering.
Smoothing choices: Full up-front true-up vs phased amortized true-up over 3 months. Tradeoff: cash collection vs customer churn/disputes risk.
Security/compliance: portability clauses must preserve data residency and audit log commitments for Private customers; requires legal review (see links).
metrics: Primary: Renewal conversion rate at T+30 and T+90
Secondary: Net Revenue Retention (NRR) 12m, number of billing disputes in renewal window, average uplift % per account
Operational: Time-to-issue-resolution for uplift disputes, support tickets created per renewal
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (pilot): 8 accounts in EMEA + 6 in NA — use weight-based allocator with 3-month smoothing
Phase 1 (experiment): Randomize 50 enterprise renewals into two uplift band treatments (2-8% and 5-12%) and control (existing flat uplift), measure 90-day outcomes
Phase 2: Incorporate signal-based allocator for accounts with > $250k ARR and run side-by-side against weight-based approach
Phase 3: Standardize contract language and ship billing automation for smoothing; update Console renewal dashboard and runbook
experiments: Experiment A: Uplift band A (low) vs control — measure renewal conversion and disputes over 90 days
Experiment B: Uplift band B (high) vs control — measure revenue, churn, and customer satisfaction
Experiment C: Weight-based vs signal-based allocator (matched accounts) — measure alignment of uplift to post-renewal usage growth
